title: Unified component variants and cost insights prototype
creator: Riley Morgan
description:
Goal: Create a cohesive set of Figma components, token mappings, and interactive prototypes that bring consistency to dashboard cards, rollout status surfaces, and cost-insight widgets across the Redwood Console.

Context: Recent audits found divergent card densities and token overrides in the deployments and billing areas. This ticket consolidates those patterns into a single source-of-truth Figma library, validates responsive behavior for embedded dashboards, and prototypes a new "Cost Insight" card family that surfaces per-model cost breakdowns, trend sparklines, and actionable rollouts links.

Scope:
- Define component families: Card (Default / Compact / Expanded), Metric Tile, Timeline / Rollout Badge, Cost Insight (summary + expanded), Empty States, Filters & Controls.
- Author token-to-component mapping: spacing, elevation, color, typographic scale, and states (idle/hover/focus/disabled).
- Build annotated Figma library with component variants and auto-layout rules.
- Build two interactive prototypes: Dashboard overview (desktop & tablet) and Rollout flow (canary -> full).
- Create a lightweight handoff sheet for engineering including CSS variables, token names, and accessibility notes.

Out of scope: Full migration of existing console screens (separate rollout). Infra work for runtime telemetry is covered by ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Figma library published with documented component variants and token mappings; 2) Desktop & tablet prototypes demonstrate responsive behavior for 3 breakpoints; 3) Cost Insight card includes: title, model key, 7-day cost sparkline, cost-per-token metric, dropdown for time range, and link to rollout; 4) Accessibility: color contrast >= 4.5:1 for key text, focus states defined, and keyboard flows documented; 5) Engineering handoff doc (Confluence) with example CSS variables and 2 example React props mapping; 6) Design review sign-off recorded and a follow-up ticket created for migration plan.
comments: 2025-11-13 - Riley Morgan: Initial exploration completed — attached three concept directions: Dense Grid (high data density), Metric-Focused (single-purpose tiles), and Narrative (story cards). Prefers Metric-Focused for early rollout due to quicker dev implementation.
2025-11-14 - Marcus Rivera (PM): Metric-Focused aligns with product goals for cost clarity. Request: include a compact variant for customers embedding the dashboard in partner apps.

2025-11-15 - Ava Chen (Designer, assignee): Built initial Figma components and token mapping. Pushed library draft and prototype links. Noted trade-off: using a single elevation token for cards simplifies platform theming but reduces per-product variety. Seeking design review on elevation decision.

2025-11-17 - Sophia Patel (Eng): Reviewed variant props. Recommendation: prefer token names with 'radius' and 'elevation' suffixes to map directly to runtime theming. Also requested that sparklines use SVG so they can be exported as an asset in the console runtime.

2025-11-18 - Design review (group): Decided to adopt token-first approach (global tokens -> component tokens -> overrides). Action: update token naming guide and add migration checklist. Request: add 2 example unit tests for visual regression (Storybook snapshots or Chromatic).

2025-11-19 - Riley Morgan: Updated prototypes per feedback. Added compact variant and keyboard navigation notes. Next: prepare Confluence handoff and create ENG migration ticket linking to this design ticket.
2025-11-20 - Ava Chen: Submitted library for final accessibility pass and requested final sign-off. Pending: PM approval of scope for migration sprint and ENG-4891 acceptance of token mappings.
